title: A Cross-lingual Comparison of Human and Classification Model Entrainment Behavior in Code-switched Speech Settings
abstract: arXiv:2607.25202v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Conversational entrainment is well-studied in monolingual and written contexts, but remains underexplored in spoken code-switching (CSW). We present a cross-lingual analysis of entrainment in Mandarin-English, Hindi-English, and Spanish-English dialogue, replicating and extending an established Spanish-English framework (Bhattacharya et al., 2024) to two new language pairs, and show that, while lexical entrainment generalizes across language pairs, entrainment over acoustic-prosodic and CSW style aspects exhibits context-specific variation. We build on these findings by asking whether classification models capture these human behavioral patterns. Using feature importance and ablation analyses, we find that classical and Transformer-based classifiers detect entrainment reasonably well but consistently prioritize features other than those most salient to human entraining behavior. translated_title: 语码转换语音场景中人类与分类模型趋同行为的跨语言比较
translated_abstract: 会话趋同在单语和书面语境中已得到充分研究，但在口语语码转换（CSW）中仍未被充分探索。我们对普通话-英语、印地语-英语和西班牙语-英语对话中的趋同行为进行了跨语言分析，将已有的西班牙语-英语研究框架（Bhattacharya et al., 2024）复制并扩展到两个新的语言对，结果表明：虽然词汇层面的趋同在不同语言对之间具有普遍性，但在声学-韵律和语码转换风格方面的趋同则表现出特定语境的变化。基于这些发现，我们进一步探讨分类模型能否捕捉这些人类行为模式。通过特征重要性和消融分析，我们发现经典分类器和基于Transformer的分类器都能较好地检测趋同现象，但它们始终优先考虑的特征并非对人类趋同行为最关键的特征。我们的方法引入了一个以人类行为为基准的框架……
tldr: 该研究首次对语码转换口语对话中的人类趋同行为进行跨语言比较，发现词汇趋同具有跨语言普遍性而声学韵律与语码转换风格趋同依赖具体语境，且分类模型虽能检测趋同但所依赖的特征与人类行为中最显著的特征并不一致。
en_tdlr: This study presents a cross-lingual comparison of human entrainment in code-switched speech, showing that lexical entrainment generalizes across language pairs while acoustic-prosodic and CSW style entrainment is context-specific, and that classifiers detect entrainment well but consistently rely on features different from those most salient to human entraining behavior.
